title: Tracing Morphology, Semantics, and Divergence in Language Acquisition
abstract: arXiv:2610.19041v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Understanding the dynamics of language acquisition in Large Language Models (LLMs) is crucial for uncovering how statistical representations evolve into structured linguistic capabilities. However, most existing studies focus primarily on fully trained models, leaving the developmental trajectory across intermediate training stages largely underexplored. In this work, we leverage intermediate checkpoints from open-source models (e.g., Pythia and OLMo) under teacher-forcing evaluation to systematically investigate language acquisition across training steps and model scales. We focus on four core characteristics: morphological structure acquisition, embedding drift, repetition dominance, and co-occurrence effects. Our findings reveal that models acquire morphological structures well before semantic embeddings stabilize. translated_title: 追踪语言习得中的形态、语义与发散
translated_abstract: 理解大语言模型（LLM）中语言习得的动态过程，对于揭示统计表示如何演变为结构化语言能力至关重要。然而，现有研究大多聚焦于完全训练好的模型，对中间训练阶段发展轨迹的探索则相对匮乏。在本工作中，我们利用开源模型（如 Pythia 和 OLMo）的中间检查点，在教师强制评估设置下，系统地研究了跨训练步骤与模型规模的语言习得过程。我们重点关注四个核心特征：形态结构习得、嵌入漂移、重复主导性以及共现效应。我们的发现表明，模型在语义嵌入趋于稳定之前就已经较好地习得了形态结构。此外，我们还发现训练数据集规模对发散识别具有积极影响，而共现对……
tldr: 该论文通过对 Pythia 和 OLMo 等开源模型中间训练检查点的系统评估，揭示了语言模型先习得形态结构、语义嵌入随后才趋于稳定的习得轨迹，并发现训练数据规模对发散识别有积极影响。
en_tdlr: By systematically evaluating intermediate checkpoints of open-source LLMs (e.g., Pythia and OLMo), this paper reveals that models acquire morphological structures well before semantic embeddings stabilize, and that training dataset size positively impacts divergence recognition.
